title: The Best Day to Buy and the Best Day to Sell

concept.title: Selling today: the best profit uses the lowest price seen so far
body: You know the price of a share for each of the next `n` days. You may buy **once** and sell **once**, and the sale must come on a later day than the purchase. What is the largest profit? If no profit is possible, the answer is 0 (you simply do not trade). For the prices `7 1 5 3 6 4` buy at 1 and sell at 6: profit 5. For `7 6 4 3 1` the prices only fall: 0.

A slow way tries every pair of days: O(n^2). Instead, think about **which day you sell**. If you sell today at price `p`, the best purchase is the **lowest price on the days before**. So walk along the days and keep `low`, the lowest price seen so far. The best profit of selling today is `p - low`, and the answer is the maximum of that over all days.

body.code:
best = 0
low = prices[0]
for p in prices:
    best = max(best, p - low)    # sell today
    low = min(low, p)            # remember the cheapest day so far
print(best)

body: `low` is a tiny DP table: `low[i]` = the minimum of the first `i + 1` prices, computed from `low[i - 1]`. The same "best so far" idea turns many quadratic loops into one pass. The time is O(n), the memory O(1).

statement: The prices of a share on `n` days are given. You may buy once and sell once, selling on a later day than buying. Print the largest profit you can make, or 0 if no profit is possible.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the number of days.
The second line has `n` numbers: the price of a share on each day.
hints: Fix the day you sell; which buying day is best?
Keep the lowest price seen so far while walking along the days.
The answer is the maximum of (price - lowest price before it), and at least 0.

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
prices = list(map(int, input().split()))

explanation: While walking along the days the lowest price so far is kept; selling today gives the profit price - lowest, and the answer is the largest such profit (at least 0).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
prices = list(map(int, input().split()))

best = 0
low = prices[0]
for p in prices:
    best = max(best, p - low)
    low = min(low, p)
print(best)
